assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration correction transformed transmission electron microscopy from a technique limited by lens defects to routine sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy, including of light atoms, interfaces, defects and in situ specimen dynamics. This is a clear instrument-driven discovery or invention with decisive, lasting consequences across materials physics, chemistry and nanoscience; the measurable resolution gain is unambiguous.
assessment.attribution: The decisive contributions are the multipole corrector designs and theory (Rose, Haider for the CEOS correctors on the TEM side) and the demonstration of aberration-corrected imaging that opened materials-science applications (Urban for the realised corrected instruments and atomic-resolution work). A three-person configuration is natural from the supplied credit; other contributors such as Zach on the scanning side or Krivanek and Dellby for STEM correctors are not in the credited list, so the allocation is not fully clean.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of development and widespread commercial adoption; many independent groups reproduce atomic-resolution results. Recognition is timely or even somewhat overdue given how deeply the method underpins modern materials analysis.
uncertainties: The credited names omit the STEM-corrector strand, so the fairness of a three-person split is debated.
Whether the committee views this as physics rather than methodology is a judgement, though the physics of electron optics is central.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED provides strong, controllable coupling of superconducting artificial atoms to microwave photons and underlies dispersive readout, gates and error-correction experiments in the leading solid-state quantum computing platforms. The idea is original, clear and has had large downstream influence.
assessment.attribution: Blais supplied the theoretical proposal with Girvin, Huang and Wallraff's group, Wallraff and Schoelkopf with colleagues realised strong coupling experimentally in 2004. The supplied credit supports a theory plus two experiment configuration, but Girvin, Devoret and others are absent from it, which complicates a fair allocation.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed across many independent laboratories and now an industrial platform. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, so this is a distinct but adjacent topic; timing is plausible though perhaps close to the previous award.
uncertainties: Overlap with the prize of the immediately preceding cycle on superconducting circuits may weigh against.
Credit between theory proposal and first experiment, and missing contributors, is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's implementations, reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and enable tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. This is a precision-measurement invention with a clear measurable outcome.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and first demonstrated strontium lattice clocks; Ye's group drove the record accuracy and many-body clock developments. A two-person award fits the supplied credit well, though Hall and Hansch were recognised earlier for the comb that is a necessary enabling tool.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent clocks worldwide agree at the 1e-18 level and international metrology bodies are moving toward redefinition; the field is mature and recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Other trapped-ion clock contributors such as Wineland were recognised in an earlier prize, and boundaries of credit between ion and lattice clocks are uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators identified a new class of phases with protected edge and surface states, tied to time-reversal symmetry and strong spin-orbit coupling. It reshaped condensed-matter physics, though the 2016 prize already recognised topological phases of matter.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the theory; Molenkamp's group gave the HgTe/CdTe experimental observation following Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's prediction. Hasan's ARPES work on three-dimensional topological insulators is a further strand, and Zhang's absence from the credited names is a notable gap, so a clean three-way split is not assured.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed by many groups using transport and ARPES; the interpretation is stable and recognition would be timely, although partially adjacent to the 2016 prize.
uncertainties: Close relation to the 2016 prize may reduce appetite.
Credit among Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Hasan and uncredited contributors is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moire engineering of flat bands, with correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable carbon system. The discovery is original and has spawned a very large subfield, including fractional Chern states.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted flat bands at a magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the experimental observation of correlated states and superconductivity in 2018. The three-name configuration follows the theory plus experiment logic, though Cao as lead author and others are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced across many groups, but the pairing mechanism and device-to-device variability remain open; some would see this as slightly early.
uncertainties: Origin of superconductivity is still debated.
Credit for the experiment extends to junior co-authors not in the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's detection of a diffuse high-energy astrophysical neutrino flux and association with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane opened neutrino astronomy as a new window. This is a large detector-driven discovery with lasting importance.
assessment.attribution: Halzen led the concept and project; Karle contributed to the detector realisation; Spiering was involved in earlier neutrino telescope development. The decisive roles are those of project leadership, which is hard to pin to three people in a very large collaboration.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly established; individual source identifications are fewer and still growing, and KM3NeT and Baikal results add independence, so the case is strong but still maturing.
uncertainties: Collaboration size and leadership roles complicate attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, and later giant values with MgO barriers, enabled hard-disk read heads and magnetic random access memory. The physics is clear and the technological impact very large.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin and, separately, Yuasa and Djayaprawira achieved giant values in crystalline MgO junctions in 2004. The credited trio is plausible but omits Yuasa, and the GMR prize of 2007 already covers a neighbouring effect.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, widely confirmed and commercialised; recognition would be timely or late.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 GMR prize and the omission of Yuasa complicate the allocation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP mapped the cosmic microwave background across the sky and fixed the parameters of the standard cosmological model to percent level, establishing precision cosmology. Importance is high, but COBE already earned the 2006 prize for the background spectrum and anisotropy.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page designed key instrument aspects and Spergel led parameter analysis. Credit in a space mission with a large team and with Planck following is difficult to focus on three people.
assessment.maturity: Results were confirmed by Planck and ground experiments, so interpretation is stable; recognition after two decades is not premature, though it is competing with the earlier award.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees an incremental advance beyond COBE.
